title: Short-Term Inflation Expectations Increase as Gas Price Growth Expectations Spike

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: The New York Fed's March 2026 Survey of Consumer Expectations shows median one-year-ahead inflation expectations rose 0.4 percentage points to 3.4%, the highest reading in recent comparison, while gas price growth expectations spiked 5.3 percentage points to 9.4%, the highest since March 2022. Labor market sentiment deteriorated with unemployment rate expectations rising to 43.5%, the highest since April 2025, while job loss fears increased and stock market optimism declined to 36.3%.
key_points: Median one-year-ahead inflation expectations increased 0.4pp to 3.4%, the largest monthly increase in recent data; three-year expectations rose 0.1pp to 3.1%; five-year remained unchanged at 3.0%
Gas price growth expectations spiked 5.3pp to 9.4%, the highest reading since March 2022; food expectations rose 0.7pp to 6.0%; rent expectations rose 1.2pp to 7.1%
Mean unemployment expectations (probability unemployment rate will be higher one year from now) increased 3.6pp to 43.5%, the highest since April 2025
Job loss probability increased 0.6pp to 14.4%; voluntary quit rate increased 2.4pp to 18.3%; earnings growth expectations decreased 0.1pp to 2.4%
Job finding probability improved 1.9pp to 45.9% across all demographics, though remaining below the 12-month trailing average of 47.5%
Probability of missing debt payments rose 0.7pp to 12.3%; households more pessimistic about current and future financial situations; expected stock price increase fell to 36.3%
why_it_matters: Rising short-term inflation expectations, particularly the spike in gas price expectations to levels not seen since early 2022, signal potential renewed inflationary pressure that could complicate Federal Reserve policy decisions. Simultaneously deteriorating labor market expectations and household financial sentiment suggest growing economic anxiety. The divergence between improving job finding optimism and rising unemployment fears suggests households may be anticipating a broad economic slowdown even as current conditions appear stable. This combination of higher-for-longer inflation expectations with deteriorating labor market confidence could influence Fed rate path expectations and market pricing.
macro_context: The survey indicates a notable shift in consumer inflation expectations with one-year-ahead median inflation expectations rising to 3.4%, the highest level since March 2022. Gas price expectations spiked to 9.4%, the highest since March 2022, suggesting households are pricing in energy cost pressures. Meanwhile, labor market sentiment deteriorated with unemployment rate expectations at 43.5%, the highest since April 2025. This combination—rising inflation expectations alongside deteriorating labor market confidence—represents a potentially challenging macro backdrop for monetary policy. The divergence between improving job finding probabilities and rising overall unemployment expectations suggests households are concerned about broad economic conditions even if current employment appears stable.
important_numbers: 43.5% mean unemployment expectations (probability rate will be higher in one year)
14.4% mean probability of job loss in next 12 months
18.3% expected quit rate in next 12 months
45.9% probability of finding a job if current job lost
5.1% median one-year-ahead household spending growth expectations
12.3% probability of missing minimum debt payment in next 3 months
36.3% probability stock prices higher 12 months from now
notes: Survey fielded March 2-31, 2026. The spike in gas price expectations to levels not seen since March 2022 represents a notable shift that could influence near-term inflation dynamics. The simultaneous rise in unemployment expectations alongside improving job finding probabilities suggests households may be differentiating between job availability and broader economic conditions. The 36.3% probability of higher stock prices one year from now represents a decline in equity market optimism. Source is a New York Fed press release covering Survey of Consumer Expectations data—a legitimate research product from the Fed's Center for Microeconomic Data. Published April 7, 2026, which is within 90 days of reference date (April 12, 2026), indicating recent data.
